newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan opposition hails budget disruption.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan opposition hails budget disruption.

text.p: Kenyan opposition activists described the disruption of Thursday's 1997/98 budget speech in parliament as "successful" and said they would soon meet to plot further action to press the government into reforms.
Willy Mutunga of the National Convention Assembly (NCA) -- which includes churches, civic groups and opposition politicians -- was pleased that Nairobi's business district was affected.

"What we did today was successful because we closed down the city," Mutunga told a news conference after opposition and ruling party members fought inside parliament in full view of President Daniel arap Moi.
Mutunga said a planned NCA demonstration to push for constitutional reforms before elections was called off because of the heavy security presence in the city.
"Today a demonstration would have been suicidal so the tactic was abandoned at the 11th hour," he said.
Opposition leader Raila Odinga told Reuters that opposition leaders would meet next week to discuss their next moves.
"Things are now begining to happen and we shall meet next Tuesday to plot our next course of action," Odinga said.
Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi doggedly read his speech but it was inaudible above the din created by shouting, stamping opposition members.
"The (finance) minister read his speech but nobody heard him at all. We managed to disrupt him and so our campaign was very successful," Odinga said.
He described 73-year-old Moi as "pensive and embarrassed" throughout the chaos in parliament.
